full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chakiader, J: This appeal by the plaintiff directed against judgment and decree dated 27-2-2001 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Additional, Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 87 of 1999 refusing to grant specific performance of a contract. 

 4. The trial Court after examining 4 witnesses for the plaintiff and 4 for defendant, found that the agreement is true and genuine but not executable as defendant did not deliver possession of the suit land to plaintiff, as such, this suit cannot be decreed and the contract cannot be executed. 

 5. Mr Md Asaduzzaman, learned. Advocate, appearing for the appellant, submits that in a suit for specific performance of a contract possession is not relevant as it decide whether the contract is genuine or not and whether the contract is executable or not, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate relied on the decision of A Jabbar Rail and others vs Sultan Hossain Matbar reported in 2006 BCR (An) ill where the Appellate Division held that in a suit for specific performance of a contract the possession is not relevant where the unregistered deed of sale is genuine document or not. 

 14. The impugned judgment and decree dated 27-2-2001 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No. 87 of 1999 is set aside. Title Suit No. 87 is decreed and defendants are directed to execute and register the Kabala Pursuant to the agreement dated 5-2-1991 within 4 (four) weeks from the date of receipt of this order failing which the Kabala will be registered in accordance with law through process of Court.
